title: SCHC Rule 7 normative definition and rule-set version diverge across artifacts
description: spec/03-adaptation.md now makes the at-least-one-UDP-endpoint-10883 Rule 7 residue normative, including AddressMode, PortDirection, and OtherPort, but the current rule-set remains version 2. The canonical appendix and Internet-Draft still describe exact-port approximately 6-byte compression, the shared vector expects zero port residue, Python and C do not implement the new form, and Rust generic rule descriptors do not model the specialized Rust codec behavior. A version-2 peer can therefore silently interpret Rule 7 under a different wire contract.
acceptance_criteria: Atomically select and document one canonical Rule 7 wire definition across spec/03-adaptation.md, appendix, Internet-Draft, vectors, Rust descriptors/selection and specialized codec, Python, and C. Preserve the old definition under v2 or increment the rule-set version everywhere required, including DIO advertisement and compatibility handling. Add byte-exact shared vectors for source-only 10883, destination-only 10883, both ports with canonical direction, link-local addresses, global addresses, mixed addresses, and malformed/noncanonical residues. Demonstrate Rust, Python, and C encode/decode identical bytes and reject incompatible rule-set versions.
notes: Post-fix correctness review: Rust still exports generic MQTT_SN_RULE descriptors whose residue is incompatible with specialized codec Rule 7, while Python generic registry has no Rule 7. Remove generic ambiguity or make all public entry points byte-identical. Draft still says ~6 bytes, says CoAP uses Rule 7, and titles Appendix A Version 1. Shared vectors need malformed/boundary cases (20/36-byte truncation, alternate modes, padding, multicast/unspecified sources, empty/max payload) consumed by every implementation.
